To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the assumption of self-interest is too narrow to account for social relationships; 2) the assumption of consequentialism, which is the core of the rationality concept, needs to be enlarged; 3) the relational behavioural principles (such as trust and reciprocity) that emerge from this enlarged conception of rationality can be fruitfully exploited in order to design more trust-enhancing incentive mechanisms; 4) the design of institutions should be based on a trust-enhancing logic.

trust is an important factor in the functioning of economic and political systems, and it is a crucial factor in the design of institutions and contracts.
